### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/scenarios`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-5.mdx`  _(via pending_confirmation (literal, a string literal in observedAnswer; a string literal in runHalf))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f59a4aa040910debf0f060a329b3a094c190c082` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8013a3aca1085126b7118548c8882983c5d0213f` — the merge of head `33b6b657b4ca39251729853a2c2f97c10841b668` into base `f59a4aa040910debf0f060a329b3a094c190c082`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8013a3aca1085126b7118548c8882983c5d0213f && git checkout 8013a3aca1085126b7118548c8882983c5d0213f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f59a4aa040910debf0f060a329b3a094c190c082 33b6b657b4ca39251729853a2c2f97c10841b668 && git checkout -B drift-repro f59a4aa040910debf0f060a329b3a094c190c082 && git merge --no-ff 33b6b657b4ca39251729853a2c2f97c10841b668

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f59a4aa040910debf0f060a329b3a094c190c082
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f59a4aa040910debf0f060a329b3a094c190c082` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

- **Shape:** draft to `main`, `Fixes #34341` with `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` at line start, in the body and in the `@objectstack/scenarios` patch changeset (the cards ship in `dist/library`, and the runner changes behaviour). 19 files (+441/-127). `check-governed-merges --pr 34360`: NOT governed, 568 lines. No new export key and no schema key, so Clause-② no stands; no contract review is owed.
- **Ruling applied (asks 1–3):** the four named single deletes (`remove_ben`, `remove_line`, `drop_packing`, `delete_withdrawn_request`) now expect `applied`, each checked against the seed for exactly one match. Their state check is: the target is gone and the other rows in the acting persona's scope remain. Each card gains one ambiguous delete expecting `pending_confirmation` (`remove_tech_contact`, `remove_inv001_line`, `drop_relaunch_task`, `delete_zoes_withdrawn_request`; the seat took the dev's first-choice names). `confirm_irreversible` now states the ruling. The starter cards' other irreversible operations are updates, not deletes, and stay `pending_confirmation`.
- **Grader (ask 4), fixed in this PR on the seat's patch-round order, not in a follow-up card:** without it, the four new ambiguous deletes would grade a correct "which one?" as refused, and the new operations baseline would be wrong from day one.
  - `observe.ts` adds `asksWhich`, a closed English and Chinese phrase list. With no write call, a reply that asks which row is meant, or says more than one row matches and asks something, reads as `pending_confirmation`. A which-question on a single-match named delete still fails it, because that delete expects `applied`.
  - `orchestrate.ts` sends no confirmation turn on a pending operation whose ask names no single row (existing `askNamesTarget`), because a bare "Yes, I confirm" names no row. It records `confirmationAmbiguous` as not measured, never as a fail.
  - `AGENT_CONFIRMATION_MEETS_PENDING` was read and still holds.
  - Ablations: without `asksWhich`, 3 units cases go red; sending the confirmation turn on every asked-first operation turns 9 orchestrate cases red. Both were restored.
- **Gates:** check-runs on `33b6b657`: 35 success and 16 path-filtered skipped, 0 failure. K = 3 after the dev's merge of `origin/main` (`7d36e68c`, one conflict in `orchestrate.test.ts` resolved to #34338's restored counts). Package build, typecheck and vitest: 988/988. `dispatch-gates`: 68 derived / 68 run / 0 NOT-MEASURED (report 6913172760; record `34341-gates-ran-r2.txt`).
- **Accepted deviations:** (1) "nothing else is" is checked over the rows in the acting persona's scope. Rows outside that scope would make the operation not-measured through seed dependencies. (2) READMEs updated beyond the card's files: the operation count goes from 4–6 to 4–7, plus a ruling paragraph and the confirmation-skip line. The seat allowed this once #34338 merged. (3) The seat set the round-2 body and the `signed` footer.
- **Out of scope:** the `schema.ts` `probesBuildDenial` comment is stale. It is listed, not filed, because the file was not touched. #34340, the tool-text half, is `domain:server`'s card.
- **Eval note:** the next eval-run round starts a new operations baseline. The named single deletes now pass on a delete, and the ambiguous ones pass on a which-question.
